name: IBM Cloudant
tagline: IBM's managed, CouchDB-compatible JSON database with built-in search and geospatial queries.
description: IBM Cloudant is a fully managed JSON document database on IBM Cloud, built on Apache CouchDB and API-compatible with it, including the replication protocol. Cloudant contributed much of CouchDB's clustering code before IBM acquired the company in 2014. On top of CouchDB it offers provisioned throughput capacity, Lucene-based full-text search, geospatial indexing, IAM integration and BYOK encryption via Key Protect, with replication across availability zones. It makes most sense for IBM Cloud shops and for apps that want CouchDB-style sync to PouchDB or on-prem CouchDB without running the cluster.

pricing.notes: Lite plan for small free usage; Standard plan billed by provisioned read/write/query throughput plus storage.

scale.notes: Data is spread across availability zones; cross-region setups use CouchDB replication between instances.

strengths: CouchDB replication means you can sync to PouchDB, CouchDB or another Cloudant
Full-text and geospatial search built in, no separate search cluster
Provisioned throughput gives predictable performance and cost
IAM and Key Protect (BYOK) integration for regulated workloads
weaknesses: Tied to IBM Cloud, which has a smaller ecosystem than AWS, Azure or GCP
Inherits CouchDB's lack of multi-document transactions
Throughput limits return 429s that apps must back off from
Fewer SDKs than in the past; older community libraries are deprecated
useCases: IoT data ingestion on IBM Cloud
Hybrid setups replicating between on-prem CouchDB and the cloud
notIdealFor: Workloads needing ACID transactions across documents
